extracted.intended_audience: research funders, fellowship selection committees, research-evaluation scholars, and policy analysts interested in peer-review selection methods
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation of committee peer-review procedures used to select doctoral and post-doctoral research fellowship recipients, with focus on measurement of reliability, fairness, and predictive validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability (agreement between reviewers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree to which different reviewers/committee members agree on award decisions; reported as percentage agreement (the paper reports 76% agreement between reviewers for fellowship award decisions). Similar reliability figures are reported for other major funding agencies' grant selection procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure inter-reviewer agreement (e.g., percent agreement, inter-rater statistics). Compare observed agreement to benchmarks from comparable funding agencies. Report reliability separately for doctoral and post-doctoral application sets and discuss implications for selection consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness (absence of systematic bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether potential sources of bias—specifically gender, nationality, major field of study, and institutional affiliation—influence selection decisions. The study found no statistically significant influence of these variables for post-doctoral applications; for doctoral applications it found evidence of institutional, major field of study, and gender bias but not nationality bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test for statistically significant associations between applicant characteristics (gender, nationality, field, institution) and selection outcomes. Disaggregate results for different fellowship types (doctoral vs post-doctoral). Use appropriate statistical controls and report where biases are present or absent; consider policy responses if biases are detected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictive validity (selection predicts future research performance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether selection decisions successfully identify the 'best' junior scientists, operationalized by subsequent bibliometric performance. The paper's bibliometric analysis showed B.I.F. fellows' research articles were cited considerably more often than the average paper in corresponding ESI journal-set fields, indicating high predictive validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess predictive validity via bibliometric indicators (citation rates) normalized to field/journal baselines (e.g., ESI categories). Compare selected recipients' citation performance to average citation rates in relevant fields. Ensure appropriate time windows for citation accumulation and consider field-normalization to avoid discipline-driven distortions.
